sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: EU–Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L561-1 to L561-51 and R561-1 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code; Article L561-45-1 of that Code (UBO register); Decree No. 2017-1094 of 13 June 2017; Order of 14 February 2023 on the Guichet Unique; EU AML Directives transposed by Ordonnance No. 2020-115 of 12 February 2020.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of shareholder passport (natural person UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or French consulate of shareholder's nationality

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (corporate shareholder, where applicable)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial/company registry of shareholder's country of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of legal representation / board resolution authorizing incorporation in France
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary/registered agent of non-French parent company

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN sanctions lists, OFAC SDN and non-SDN sectoral sanctions, French national restrictive measures administered by the Direction générale du Trésor (DG Trésor), and Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) using a risk-based approach per Article L561-10 of the Monetary and Financial Code. Continuous monitoring is required under Article L561-6 before establishment of the business relationship and throughout the formation process.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises (INPI; formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name (dénomination sociale) may be in any language but must be stated in Latin alphabet; non-Latin scripts require a transliteration filed with the registrar. The name must be noticeably distinct from existing RNE/INPI national company names and prior trademarks; the instructions for the legal form 'SARL' and registered capital are mandatory.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Guichet unique registers a rejection of the proposed name on grounds of prior rights or public order, the applicant may within 15 days submit a formal request for reconsideration to the same registry portal, attaching substantiating evidence of non-confusion (e.g., trademark coexistence consent or similar-name search report). If rejection is persevered, the applicant may petition the President of the Tribunal de Commerce in référé proceedings or, failing that, choose a new distinct name and refile. Administrative appeals against registry refusals are governed by Articles R210-1 to R210-10 of the French Commercial Code.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are not accepted as the sole statutory seat for a SARL. However, a commercial domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) registered with the French authorities may be used, subject to a written lease/service agreement, on-site support, and registration of the domiciliation address with the commercial registry. A home office at the manager's French residence is also permissible.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: French SARL pre-incorporation legal consultation and drafting of articles (Statuts)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark; no statutory tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name availability and trademark clearance search (différenciation and infringement check)
Publication of legal announcement of incorporation (annonce légale)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Approved legal announcement newspaper (Journal d'annonces légales)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per line/article under Code de commerce Article R210-9

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Guichet unique filing (RNE registration, KBIS and SIREN/SIRET management)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI (Institut national de la propriété industrielle)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff set by INPI order

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial register formalities and registration at Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory greffe fees and taxes fixed by decree

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, apostille and translation of foreign UBO/corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary/translator and apostille office in country of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing notarial tariff and language service benchmark

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code, Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 and R.223-1 to R.223-36 concerning sociétés à responsabilité limitée; Articles L.123-1 et seq. concerning business registration; French Civil Code Articles 1832 et seq. concerning companies and contributions.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre national des entreprises administered by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI), with commercial registration recorded in the Registre du commerce et des sociétés by the competent local commercial court registry (greffe du tribunal de commerce).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic declaration of company formation submitted through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises, replacing the former M0 form, together with the signed articles of association and required supporting documents.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital applies; EUR 1 is legally sufficient, subject to adequate capitalization. For cash contributions, at least 20% must be paid upon incorporation and the balance within five years. Paid-in cash is normally deposited in a blocked bank or notarial account, and the deposit certificate is filed for registration. The incorporation filing fee excludes legal-notice publication, beneficial-owner filing, bank charges, and professional fees. The USD amount is an indicative conversion of the applicable commercial registry fee and is exchange-rate dependent.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The first management resolution of [Company Name] SARL is adopted on [date]. The Company accepts the subscription by each shareholder of the quotas specified in the articles of association and acknowledges payment of the required initial cash contributions into the designated capital account. The registered office is established at [full French address]. [Name] is appointed gérant for an indefinite term, subject to the articles and applicable law. The gérant is authorized to sign incorporation filings, obtain the registration extract, open operating bank and payment accounts, appoint accountants and advisers, and complete all ancillary formalities before the INPI, RCS, tax administration, banks, and payment-service providers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm corporate identity, activities, and registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises; competent local commercial court registry for RCS jurisdiction
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the company name, SARL form, business purpose, ISIC/NAF activity description, shareholders, manager, capital amount, ownership percentages, and French registered-office address. Obtain proof of premises, domiciliation agreement, or host certificate. Ensure the proposed activity accurately describes online retail of made-to-order apparel and does not imply in-house manufacturing if production is outsourced.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and business purpose
Executed domiciliation agreement or lease, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct the activity wording, address evidence, identity data, or beneficial-owner information before submission. Obtain a replacement domiciliation document if the registry rejects the premises evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare, execute, and publish the incorporation documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Accredited journal habilité à publier des annonces légales in the registered-office department; private notary or qualified legal adviser where notarization is voluntarily used
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the French articles of association, capital table, appointment of the gérant, and beneficial-owner declaration. Execute the articles by all shareholders. Deposit the incorporation notice with an authorized legal-announcement journal and retain the attestation de parution. Notarization is generally not required for standard cash-capital SARL formation, but documents signed abroad may require legalization or apostille and certified French translations.
required_dossiers: Non-conviction and parentage declaration of the gérant
Certified French translations and apostilles, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Republish any defective legal notice and amend inconsistent articles or appointment documents before electronic filing. Cure signature, translation, apostille, or date defects through the issuing professional.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit share capital and obtain the bank certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French bank, payment institution permitted to receive corporate capital, or French notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital account in the name of the company being formed. Transfer the subscribed cash contributions, obtain the certificat de dépôt des fonds, and attach it to the incorporation dossier. The account remains restricted until registration, after which the registration extract is provided to release the funds into the operating account.
required_dossiers: Source-of-funds information requested under AML procedures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to bank KYC or source-of-funds queries, replace incomplete identification documents, and obtain a written refusal if the bank declines. Use another eligible bank, payment institution, or notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create the electronic filing, select company creation and SARL, complete the legal, tax, social, activity, premises, manager, shareholder, and beneficial-owner sections, upload clear PDF documents, sign electronically, pay applicable charges, and retain the filing receipt. Select the appropriate tax regime and identify any foreign shareholders or managers accurately.
required_dossiers: Manager identity, acceptance, and non-conviction declaration
Power of attorney, if filed by an agent
Foreign identity documents and certified translations, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Monitor the INPI dashboard and respond within the stated deadline to any formal query. Upload corrected documents through the portal, preserve the original submission receipt, and request review by the competent registry if the status is incorrectly closed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain registration evidence and activate corporate operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Competent commercial court registry, INPI, French tax administration, and URSSAF
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After approval, obtain the extrait Kbis or equivalent RCS registration evidence, SIREN and SIRET numbers, and APE/NAF classification. Provide the registration extract to the bank to release capital. Activate the operating account, payment-service accounts, accounting records, VAT processes, payroll registrations if applicable, and mandatory website consumer-law information.
required_dossiers: Employment registrations, if personnel are hired
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct post-registration data through the INPI amendment procedure or the competent registry. Contact the tax office or URSSAF for account activation issues and retain evidence of all submissions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Implement SARL governance and recurring compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company gérant, shareholders, competent commercial court registry, tax administration, and URSSAF
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Maintain the quota register, shareholder decisions, accounting records, annual accounts, and management report where required. Hold the annual shareholder approval meeting within six months after financial year-end, approve the accounts, allocate profit, and file annual accounts when legally required. Report changes in manager, registered office, ownership, beneficial ownership, or activity through the INPI portal.
required_dossiers: Annual accounts and management report, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Submit corrective amendments, late filings, or replacement accounts through the competent portal or registry. Rectify shareholder resolutions and seek professional advice where a missed deadline affects statutory approval or filing validity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable to ordinary online print-on-demand apparel retailing without an owned manufacturing facility. If the company operates a regulated production or storage installation, the competent authority is the prefecture, supported by the relevant regional Directorate for Environment, Planning and Housing (Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement; DREAL), under the classified-installations regime.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No general operating or manufacturing permit is required for an online POD retail business using third-party production. A regulated workshop or industrial installation may require an ICPE declaration, registration, or authorization under the French Environmental Code, depending on the activity and thresholds.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: French Environmental Authority (Autorité environnementale), with regional DREAL services and the competent prefecture
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally exempt from project-level EIA for online retail with outsourced production and no industrial premises. A full environmental assessment or case-by-case screening may apply if the company constructs or operates a qualifying ICPE installation, materially handles chemicals, or undertakes a listed development project.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No dedicated wastewater, VOC, or industrial-emissions thresholds apply to ordinary office and e-commerce operations. Any owned printing, dyeing, coating, or finishing site must comply with applicable ICPE requirements, water-discharge conditions, air-emission limits, chemical-storage rules, hazardous-waste controls, waste-traceability obligations, and municipal sewer authorization. Outsourced manufacturers remain responsible for their regulated emissions, subject to contractual compliance verification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No general pre-opening industrial clearance applies to a virtual retail business. A public-facing premises may be an établissement recevant du public and require municipal fire-safety and accessibility compliance, with commission review where applicable. Any warehouse or workshop must satisfy fire-prevention, emergency-access, electrical, structural-load, machinery, and occupational-health requirements. The employer must prepare and maintain the Document unique d'évaluation des risques professionnels, provide required training and protective measures, and complete workplace inspections or certifications required by the premises and equipment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – foreign business desk: Service des Impôts des Entreprises Étrangères (SIEE), Noisy-le-Grand; portal: impots.gouv.fr / portailpro.gouv.fr. Business formalities and VAT registration are routed through the Guichet unique formalités (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) and the Centre de Formalités des Entreprises (CFE).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SARL receives a SIREN/SIRET number automatically upon incorporation, along with a VAT intra-community number (FR + SIREN-based key) from DGFiP. For a foreign entity establishing a branch or selling in France, submit French VAT registration (form 1547 – 'procédure simplifiée de régularisation') to the SIEE, attaching proof of existence, original power of attorney, and a projection of French turnover. Non-resident businesses have a zero registration threshold: VAT registration is required from the first taxable supply in France, unless the supplies are covered by the EU One-Stop Shop (OSS) regime for distance sales.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not operate a 'check-the-box' regime. A small SARL may elect income-tax transparency (imposition à l'impôt sur le revenu – IR) for up to five fiscal years under CGI 239 bis AB, subject to turnover and ownership ceilings. No other elective hybrid classification exists. France applies ATTAD/hybrid mismatch adjustment rules under CGI 212 bis, which are mandatory and do not constitute an election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA / French VAT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Domestic small-business 'franchise en base' exemption: EUR 85,800 annual taxable turnover for goods (retail POD apparel) and EUR 37,500 for services; figures apply to established French entities. Non-established suppliers have a zero threshold – registration is mandatory from the first taxable supply unless OSS or an EU import scheme applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory French e-invoicing reform deployed in stages: from 1 September 2026, large and medium enterprises must issue structured electronic invoices (FACTUR-X / Peppol BIS) via an approved PDP or the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF); from 1 September 2027, all SMEs including SARL must receive and issue e-invoices. Concurrently, transaction data must be transmitted to DGFiP through the PPF for audit and VAT-filing purposes. Retail POD B2C transactions require NF 525-compliant cash-register software or invoicing system; no real-time fiscal stamping applies to sales invoices, but customs export declarations must be filed electronically using the DELTA-G clearance system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rate VAT applies to goods physically dispatched or transported outside the European Union by the seller within three months of the transfer of ownership or dispatch. Qualifying conditions: the exporter holds a customs export declaration (DAE) accepted in DELTA-G, transport documents proving departure from the EU (e.g., Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, CMR), a commercial invoice, and a signed purchase contract/payment record. For POD custom apparel, the SARL may zero-rate the supply if it directly exports the finished articles to a non-EU consumer or business. Electronically supplied services to non-EU consumers are outside the scope of French VAT rather than zero-rated. Export evidence must be retained for at least ten years (CGI art. 286-3).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAE / DELTA-G) with EX-EAES / ETS acceptance number
Bill of Lading (original sea freight) or Air Waybill (air freight) evidencing physical removal from the EU
Commercial invoice / sales contract and payment receipt

Inward Remittance Certificate (attestation de rapatriement de recettes d'exportation) required by French foreign-exchange controls where export proceeds exceed EUR 12,500 or the 180-day repatriation deadline applies
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If export proof is incomplete or false, DGFiP recovers the unpaid VAT at the standard 20% rate plus late-interest at 0.05% per month and raises penalties: up to 80% of the tax under bad faith (mauvaise foi) or 100% for organised dissimulation (manœuvre frauduleuse). Customs authorities may impose parallel fines and seize goods. Criminal liability for customs or VAT export fraud reaches fines up to EUR 500,000 and ten years' imprisonment for organised fraud. The ordinary reassessment period is six years; in cases of tax abuse (abus de droit) the clawback window can extend to ten years. Export records must be made available for electronic audit upon DGFiP demand.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France; foreign exchange administration and balance-of-payments oversight: Direction Générale du Trésor (DG Trésor), Ministry of Economic, Financial and Industrial Sovereignty
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France maintains full euro convertibility under EU free movement of capital. Both current-account transactions (trade in goods/services, royalties, intra-group fees) and capital-account transactions (equity subscription, shareholder loans, dividend remittances) are unrestricted. There are no administrative FX approvals for profit remittances; the only constraints arise from corporate law solvency tests, beneficial-ownership disclosure, tax withholding/reporting, and EU/UN sanctions screening.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender regime exists for French exporters. Export receivables in convertible currencies may be kept in foreign-currency accounts or converted at freely negotiated rates without any compulsory timeline or conversion ratio. Export proceeds must be recorded in Banque de France balance-of-payments statistics when individual transaction thresholds are met, but no repatriation certificate or government consent is required.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account for multi-currency treasury

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: High for EU/EEA-authorized e-money or payment institutions (EMIs/PIs) passporting into France under PSD2 with an ACPR-registered agent; Low-to-Feasible only via partner bank sponsorship for offshore/non-EEA EMIs. An offshore digital EMI cannot directly open a French IBAN or settle payment services for a French SARL; it may process retail card payouts, but the SARL should maintain its primary settlement account at an ACPR-licensed bank or a passported EU EMI to avoid treasury isolation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is possible for EU-resident legal representatives and UBOs using eIDAS qualified electronic signatures and secure video KYC, but most first-tier French banks require a physical interview or a notarized/consular-validated appointment for non-resident directors and beneficial owners, particularly when the SARL is in pre-revenue or cross-border POD mode. A power of attorney executed under French notarial formalities and apostilled (if non-EU) is needed for signatory delegation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO ownership chain incomplete or opaque due to offshore/trust structures in print-on-demand funding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized UBO register for the SARL, full legal-entity ownership chart, direct and indirect ownership percentages, identity documents for each UBO, and a signed declaration confirming no undeclared nominee holdings.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection disproportionate to stated e-commerce activity or to registered share capital.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder resolution approving capital increase or current-account advance, audited source-of-funds documentation from the contributor (bank statements, income-tax returns, financial statements), and a cash-flow forecast aligning injection amounts with POD inventory, fulfilment and marketing costs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border supplier payments to jurisdictions perceived as high-risk for money laundering or diverted customs.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial invoices, Incoterms and Customs export/import status (ENS/D.A.U./desk-dispatch records), supplier AML/KYB questionnaire with UBO certificates, and evidence of physical logistics movement from factory to fulfilment centre.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Aggregate payout volume from Stripe, PayPal or offshore gateways triggering unexplained-wealth or tax-red flag reviews.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Reconciled payout reports from all payment aggregators, e-commerce order-level transaction logs, VAT/OSS returns, ERP revenue-recognition records, and customer refund/dispute ledgers.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For euro inbound wires from the EU/EEA, use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant with the exact SARL IBAN and legal name. For extra-EEA injections, use SWIFT MT103 with a Unique End-to-End Transaction Reference (UETR), a clear purpose code such as 'Capital Social' or 'Apport en Compte Courant d'Associé', and full originator KYC information. Verification: counterparty bank must execute risk-based checks on source-of-funds; the French receiving bank will require the corporate authorization (rib-document, share-resolution) and may ask for a sworn statement of 'capitaux propres' if the injection is classified as a shareholder loan. Tolerance and final validation require matching beneficiary legal name exactly to the bank mandate and RNE UBO record.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer / SEPA Instant for euro settlements with EU suppliers; use SWIFT MT103 with UETR for intercontinental POD raw-material and freight payments; and use irrevocable documentary letters of credit (Commercial LC) for high-value bespoke manufacturing contracts where provisional invoicing and customs status require banker's undertaking. Maintain separate payment rails for duty/VAT remittance to the French customs authority and for supplier payments; retain each transaction's supporting commercial invoice, proof-of-delivery, and customs declaration.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forwards (plain vanilla) to lock conversion rates on anticipated USD/GBP or other trade payables/receivables
FX Options (vanilla puts/calls) to hedge adverse currency movements without fully waiving upside
Cross-currency swaps (FX swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps) for matched funding and repayment structures
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies subject to convertibility restrictions in the counterparty country
Foreign-currency cash accounts for natural hedging of euro-USD/GBP operating cash-flow gaps

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year accounts, by the second working day after 1 May; for off-year accounts, within 3 months of the financial year close.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late-filing penalty plus 0.2% monthly interest; after formal notice, assessment may be made ex officio; repeated default may lead to tax enforcement action.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Final corporate income tax payment (solde IS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year accounts, by 15 May; for off-year accounts, by the 15th day of the fourth month following the financial year close.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Immediate 10% increase, increased to 40% after 3 months, plus 0.2% monthly late interest; enforced by garnishment or asset seizure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual accounts (dépôt des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce of the registered office jurisdiction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the financial year close; for 31 December year-end, by 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal notice, then coercive fine (astreinte) up to EUR 150/day; criminal fine up to EUR 4,500 for directors; persistent non-filing triggers administrative strike-off (radiation) after formal notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Update of the declaration of beneficial owners (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days of any change in beneficial ownership; no annual no-change filing is required under French law.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine up to EUR 7,500 for individuals and EUR 37,500 for legal entities; company may be ordered to rectify the register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local economic contribution (Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable annually by 15 December; first-year exemption for newly created companies in respect of premises newly occupied.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% increase if unpaid as of 31 December, 40% after 3 months, plus 0.2% monthly late interest; recovery through tax execution procedures.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A SARL must appoint a statutory auditor when it exceeds at least two of the following thresholds at a financial year end: total balance sheet EUR 2,365,000, net turnover excluding VAT EUR 4,724,000, and 25 employees. Appointment is also mandatory if requested by members holding at least one tenth of the share capital.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général under ANC règlement n°2014-03); IFRS is mandatory for consolidated financial statements of listed groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not require an annual stand-alone UBO confirmation. The beneficial owner information must be kept continuously accurate, and any shareholding transfer creating a change in beneficial ownership must be declared to the commercial court registry within 15 days. The register of beneficial owners must be held at the registered office and shown to authorised authorities on request.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of share transfers (registre des mouvements de titres)
Minutes of shareholders' meetings and resolutions
Register of beneficial owners (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés). Eligible small companies may apply a 15% rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to French ownership, turnover, and paid-in-capital conditions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The standard rate is 25%. The reduced 15% SME rate may apply to qualifying companies with annual turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million and qualifying capital ownership. Corporate tax installments are generally payable on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December, with the final balance generally due by the 15th day of the fourth month following year-end. France generally provides unlimited carryforward of tax losses, subject to an annual utilization cap of EUR 1 million plus 50% of the portion of current-year taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million. Loss carryback is generally limited to the immediately preceding fiscal year and capped at the lower of the preceding year's profit or EUR 1 million.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD, corporate income tax return, with financial schedules 2050-SD through 2059-SD and applicable tax-credit schedules, filed electronically through the French tax administration's professional portal impots.gouv.fr using EDI-TDFC or EFI where available.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; corporate income tax installments and balance payments are generally quarterly or event-driven, using Form 2571-SD for installments and Form 2572-SD for the balance.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return is generally due within three months after the end of the fiscal year. For a fiscal year ending on 31 December, the ordinary deadline is the second business day after 1 May of the following year. Payment of the final balance is generally due by the 15th day of the fourth month following year-end. Electronic filing is mandatory for French companies subject to corporate income tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, SIREN number, registered office, fiscal year dates, legal form, tax office, and activity classification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the French permanent establishment or subsidiary details. A non-resident shareholder is not entered as the taxpayer unless it directly operates a French taxable presence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit or tax loss, applicable corporate tax rate, gross corporate tax, credits, reductions, and net tax payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only French-source taxable income attributable to the French SARL. Do not deduct foreign head-office expenses unless properly allocated, documented, and legally deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fixed assets, inventory, trade receivables, cash, prepaid expenses, and other assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Record assets legally or economically attributable to the French entity. Related-party balances must reconcile with intercompany ledgers and transfer-pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Share capital, reserves, retained earnings, provisions, borrowings, trade payables, tax liabilities, and other liabilities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose shareholder loans and related-party financing separately where required. Thin-capitalization and interest-deduction limitations must be tested.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenue, purchases, payroll, external expenses, depreciation, provisions, finance income and expense, exceptional items, and accounting profit or loss.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: French turnover must be reconciled to VAT returns, payment-platform reports, customs records, and statutory accounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent and temporary add-backs, non-deductible expenses, tax-exempt income, depreciation adjustments, provisions, and other tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back non-deductible foreign parent charges, unsupported royalties, excessive management fees, penalties, and expenses lacking a French business purpose.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Losses carried forward, losses carried back, current-year loss, and utilization of prior losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the French annual loss-utilization cap and retain schedules supporting the origin, amount, and continuity of each loss.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income, group or consolidation adjustments where applicable, and final taxable base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A standalone SARL generally reports its own French taxable base. French tax consolidation requires separate eligibility and election conditions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Debt-related information and, where applicable, data relevant to interest limitation and related-party financing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify cross-border shareholder loans, lenders, interest rates, guarantees, maturity, currency, and arm's-length support.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and reductions, including research, innovation, apprenticeship, or other qualifying credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only credits supported by French eligibility conditions, contemporaneous records, and documentary evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax installments paid during the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate installments against the preceding or estimated current-year liability and reconcile them to the annual return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax balance, overpayment, or amount refundable after crediting installments and tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File and pay the balance by the applicable statutory deadline, even where the annual return is filed separately.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or incomplete filing generally triggers a 10% surcharge, increasing to 40% for deliberate non-compliance and up to 80% for fraudulent conduct or abusive concealment. Late payment generally bears default interest at 0.20% per month, subject to statutory rules. Failure to use mandatory electronic filing may trigger a separate surcharge. Repeated or serious failures may lead to tax audits, estimated assessment, loss of evidentiary protection, and criminal referral.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% French withholding tax generally applies to dividends and similar distributions paid by a French company to a non-resident, subject to applicable treaty relief, EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief, and anti-abuse conditions. French resident individual shareholders may be subject to a separate personal tax regime rather than the non-resident dividend withholding regime.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain valid beneficial-owner and residence documentation from the recipient and assess the applicable double tax agreement, EU directive, principal-purpose test, anti-conduit rules, and minimum holding conditions. Use the applicable French forms, generally Form 5000 for residence and treaty entitlement and Form 5001 for dividend income, where required. Submit certified forms to the French payer, custodian, or tax authority within the prescribed timing. The French payer remains responsible for correct withholding, remittance, reporting, and retention of evidence. Refund claims may be filed where relief was not obtained at source.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French-source royalties paid to non-residents may generally be subject to 25% withholding, subject to treaty reduction, EU Interest and Royalties Directive exemption, beneficial-ownership requirements, and anti-abuse rules. Ordinary interest paid by a French company to a non-resident is generally not subject to French withholding tax, but special rules may apply to payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions, certain debt instruments, or payments recharacterized as distributions. Treaty rates must be confirmed under the specific bilateral convention.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full transfer-pricing documentation, including Local File and Master File obligations for qualifying entities or French groups, generally applies where annual pre-tax turnover or gross assets reach at least EUR 400 million, or where the entity is controlled by or controls an enterprise meeting the EUR 400 million threshold. A separate simplified transfer-pricing declaration generally applies from the EUR 50 million turnover or gross-assets threshold, subject to statutory conditions and current filing rules.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no single standalone economic-substance regulation equivalent to some offshore ESR regimes. Substance is enforced through the arm's-length principle, abuse-of-law doctrine, principal-purpose testing, beneficial-ownership rules, controlled foreign company rules, permanent-establishment principles, anti-hybrid rules, interest limitation, and general deductibility requirements. A French SARL should maintain French decision-making, personnel or outsourced operational capacity, premises or documented operational infrastructure, accounting records, commercial rationale, inventory and fulfillment evidence, and board and management records proportionate to its POD retail functions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent tax reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately concealing French sales, omitting payment-platform receipts, falsifying invoices, claiming fictitious expenses, or materially understating taxable income or VAT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, 40% surcharge for deliberate conduct, up to 80% surcharge for fraudulent maneuvers or abusive concealment, default interest at 0.20% per month, and potential criminal tax-fraud penalties of up to five years' imprisonment and EUR 500,000 fine. Aggravated cases can reach seven years' imprisonment and EUR 3 million fine, subject to statutory conditions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may incur criminal liability where they personally participated in the conduct. Courts may impose civil restitution, damages, asset seizure, management bans, and other judicial restrictions. Travel restrictions are not automatic but may arise from judicial-control measures or criminal proceedings. A court may impose director liability for unpaid tax where serious and repeated management misconduct caused the company's tax insolvency.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to register or account for French VAT, misapplying distance-sale rules, using incorrect OSS/IOSS treatment, issuing false VAT invoices, or claiming input VAT without genuine supplies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT assessment, interest, penalties generally ranging from 10% to 80% depending on conduct, denial of input-tax recovery, joint-liability measures in qualifying cases, and criminal prosecution for organized or fraudulent conduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be prosecuted for intentional participation and may face fines, imprisonment in aggravated cases, asset seizure, management prohibition, and civil contribution claims. Travel bans are case-specific and not an automatic consequence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using non-arm's-length royalties, management fees, procurement charges, financing, or inventory prices to shift POD profits from France without functional analysis or supporting evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income-tax reassessment, withholding-tax exposure, interest, 10% documentation-related penalty where applicable, 40% or 80% tax penalties for intentional or fraudulent conduct, and possible denial of deductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face liability for deliberate misstatements or fraudulent documentation. Civil restitution, management bans, and criminal sanctions may apply where conduct constitutes tax fraud or falsification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a nominal French SARL with no genuine commercial activity, using nominee management, routing sales through France solely to obtain treaty benefits, or claiming French operations unsupported by personnel, infrastructure, or decision-making.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty or directive benefits, reallocation of profits, permanent-establishment findings, tax reassessment, abuse-of-law penalties up to 80%, withholding-tax recovery, and potential criminal referral where documents or declarations are fraudulent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally exposed for fraudulent implementation, asset diversion, or serious management misconduct. Civil claims, asset seizure, management bans, and imprisonment may apply where separate criminal offenses are established. Travel restrictions require judicial action.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain or accurately file beneficial-owner information, accepting unexplained funds, concealing the ultimate owner, structuring payments, or failing to report suspicious activity through the regulated payment or financial channel.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate and individual administrative or criminal sanctions, beneficial-owner registration enforcement, account restrictions, confiscation, AML fines, and potential imprisonment depending on the underlying offense.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may be personally liable for knowing participation, concealment, or failure to implement required controls. Asset confiscation, civil restitution, management prohibition, judicial-control travel restrictions, and imprisonment may apply according to the offense.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using Stripe or PayPal accounts belonging to another entity, splitting transactions to conceal turnover, issuing invoices from an offshore entity while French operations perform the sale, or failing to reconcile platform statements with French accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, VAT and corporate-tax penalties, withholding-tax exposure, bookkeeping sanctions, potential seizure of records and funds, and criminal fraud or forgery penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may face criminal liability, civil restitution, asset seizure, management bans, and imprisonment where fraud, forgery, or money laundering is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Undisclosed related-party financing and profit extraction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Making undocumented shareholder loans, excessive interest payments, disguised dividends, unsupported capital withdrawals, or payments to related parties in low-tax jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Interest limitation, recharacterization as distributions, withholding-tax recovery, corporate-tax reassessment, penalties, and potential application of anti-abuse and non-cooperative-jurisdiction rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for misuse of corporate assets, fraudulent bankruptcy conduct, or deliberate tax evasion. Civil restitution, asset seizure, management bans, and imprisonment may apply to proven criminal conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to preserve accounting and tax records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Inadequate French accounting books, missing inventory and fulfillment evidence, destroyed electronic records, unsupported expense claims, or inability to reproduce audit trails for online orders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Estimated assessment, rejection of deductions and input VAT, penalties for incomplete or inaccurate declarations, audit extensions, and potential criminal consequences for concealment or falsification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may be personally responsible for intentional destruction or falsification of records and may face civil claims, management bans, asset seizure, and imprisonment where a criminal offense is established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends without distributable reserves, extracting assets while unable to pay taxes or creditors, continuing trading after insolvency, or preferring connected creditors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Dividend recovery, creditor claims, insolvency proceedings, director contribution to liabilities, asset-recovery actions, management bans, and potential bankruptcy-related criminal sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be ordered to contribute to all or part of the company's liabilities where serious management misconduct caused insufficiency of assets. Fraudulent bankruptcy may result in criminal fines, imprisonment, asset seizure, and judicial management prohibition. Travel restrictions are discretionary and case-specific.
